//: What the road rules say about every draft this repo has actually
recorded. tests/test_road_corpus_diff.py compares the rules against it.
The point is regressions against REAL copy rather than invented cases. A
unit test only asks what you thought to ask; this asks what the forecaster
actually wrote. It is how the 'this evening' regression was caught during
PR #37 -- extending a rule to route numbers and a bare trailing 'this'
silently re-broke 2026-09-22, one of the four drafts whose lint failure
started that work, and no unit test noticed.
Only the files listed here are checked, so the daily workflow commits that
add new drafts do not turn this red. A file that disappears is skipped.
flagged=false is the load-bearing half: those are sentences the rules must
keep leaving alone. flagged=true entries pin the sentence, so a rule that
stops catching a known violation, or starts catching a different part of
the same draft, shows up as a diff rather than as an unchanged count.
To refresh after an INTENDED behaviour change:
and read the diff before committing it -- that diff is the review.
